_about: The church side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of the people gathered that more than one book shares, from the assembly of the LORD in Israel to the Gospels and the letters, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: The assembly of the LORD

The Law & history: on the day of the assembly
may enter the assembly of the LORD
may enter the assembly of the LORD
No Ammonite or Moabite or any of their descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD
may enter the assembly of the LORD
the whole congregation of the LORD
all Israel, the assembly of the LORD
no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God
The Prophets: those You had forbidden to enter Your assembly
you will have no one in the assembly of the LORD
Gospels & Acts: He was in the assembly in the wilderness

rows.alike: Most name the gathered people as the LORD's own: "the assembly of the LORD", "the LORD's assembly", "the congregation of the LORD", "the assembly of God".
rows.different: Deuteronomy 23 sets out who "may enter the assembly of the LORD"; Nehemiah 13:1 finds read aloud that "no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God", and Lamentations 1:10 speaks of the nations as "those You had forbidden to enter Your assembly". Micah 2:5 says "you will have no one in the assembly of the LORD to divide the land by lot"; Acts 7:38 has "He was in the assembly in the wilderness" and Deuteronomy 9:10 "on the day of the assembly".

rows.title: The church of God

Gospels & Acts: Be shepherds of the church of God
But Saul began to destroy the church
The letters: To the church of God in Corinth
To the church of God in Corinth
whether to Jews or Greeks or the church of God
nor do the churches of God
do you despise the church of God
because I persecuted the church of God
how severely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it
To the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
To the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
the churches of God in Judea that are in Christ Jesus
how can he care for the church of God?
the church of the living God

rows.alike: Acts 20:28 and the letters both say "the church of God", and the letters also "the churches of God" and "God's churches".
rows.different: Acts 8:3 says "Saul began to destroy the church"; in the letters the writer says "I persecuted the church of God", and Galatians 1:13 adds "and tried to destroy it". 1 Timothy 3:15 has "the church of the living God"; 1 Thessalonians 1:1 writes "To the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ", and 1 Thessalonians 2:14 "the churches of God in Judea that are in Christ Jesus".

rows.title: Praise in the assembly

The Law & history: Then David blessed the LORD in the sight of all the assembly
Psalms & wisdom: I will praise You in the assembly
My praise for You resounds in the great assembly
in the congregations I will bless the LORD
Then I will give You thanks in the great assembly
I proclaim righteousness in the great assembly
I have not concealed Your loving devotion and faithfulness from the great assembly
Bless God in the great congregation
The heavens praise Your wonders, O LORD-Your faithfulness as well-in the assembly of the holy ones
Let them exalt Him in the assembly of the people
I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart in the council of the upright and in the assembly
His praise in the assembly of the godly
The letters: I will sing Your praises in the assembly

rows.alike: Praise is given before the gathered people: "I will praise You in the assembly" (Psalm 22:22), "I will sing Your praises in the assembly" (Hebrews 2:12), "in the great assembly", "His praise in the assembly of the godly".
rows.different: Hebrews 2:12 has "sing Your praises" where Psalm 22:22 has "praise You", and sets the words after "He says". Psalm 40 has "I proclaim righteousness" rather than praise; in Psalm 89:5 it is "The heavens" that praise, "in the assembly of the holy ones"; 1 Chronicles 29:10 tells of David who "blessed the LORD in the sight of all the assembly".

rows.title: Your congregation, which You purchased

The Law & history: until the people You have bought pass by
Psalms & wisdom: Remember Your congregation, which You purchased long ago and redeemed as the tribe of Your inheritance
Gospels & Acts: the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood
The letters: you were bought at a price
You were bought at a price
denying the Master who bought them
Revelation: by Your blood You purchased for God those from every tribe and tongue and people and nation

rows.alike: Each speaks of those who were bought: "the people You have bought", "Your congregation, which You purchased", "the church of God, which He purchased", "you were bought at a price", "You purchased for God".
rows.different: Exodus 15:16 and Psalm 74:2 are addressed to God, and the Psalm adds "long ago" and "redeemed as the tribe of Your inheritance"; Acts 20:28 has "with His own blood" and Revelation 5:9 "by Your blood", with "those from every tribe and tongue and people and nation". 1 Corinthians says only "at a price" and goes on with "Therefore glorify God with your body" and "do not become slaves of men"; 2 Peter 2:1 speaks of false teachers "denying the Master who bought them".

rows.title: Here are My mother and My brothers

Psalms & wisdom: I will proclaim Your name to my brothers
Gospels & Acts: Here are My mother and My brothers
whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother
Here are My mother and My brothers!
whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother
My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out
whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me
Go and tell My brothers to go to Galilee
But go and tell My brothers
The letters: So Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers
I will proclaim Your name to My brothers

rows.alike: The speaker calls others "My brothers": "Here are My mother and My brothers", "Go and tell My brothers", "I will proclaim Your name to My brothers".
rows.different: Each Gospel names who they are differently: "whoever does the will of My Father in heaven" (Matthew), "whoever does the will of God" (Mark), "those who hear the word of God and carry it out" (Luke); Matthew 25:40 has "the least of these brothers of Mine". Matthew 28:10 and John 20:17 send word: "Go and tell My brothers", "go and tell My brothers". Hebrews 2:11 says "Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers", and 2:12 follows with "He says".

rows.title: A chosen people, a holy nation

The Law & history: You are to be My holy people
For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you
for you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD has chosen you
For you are a holy people belonging to the LORD your God
you will be a holy people to the LORD your God, as He has promised
The LORD will establish you as His holy people, just as He has sworn to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God
Psalms & wisdom: the people He has chosen as His inheritance
The Prophets: to give drink to My chosen people
they will be called the Holy People
He will destroy the mighty men along with the holy people
When the power of the holy people has finally been shattered

rows.alike: "a holy nation" stands in Exodus 19:6 and 1 Peter 2:9; "a people holy to the LORD your God" and "His holy people" in Deuteronomy; "My chosen people" in Isaiah 43:20 and "a chosen people" in 1 Peter 2:9.
rows.different: Exodus 19:6 is given as "the words that you are to speak to the Israelites"; Deuteronomy 7:6 says "The LORD your God has chosen you", and Deuteronomy 28:9 has "if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God". 1 Peter 2:9 has "But you are a chosen people" and "to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light". In Daniel "the holy people" are spoken of under attack: "He will destroy the mighty men along with the holy people".

rows.title: His chosen ones, the elect

The Law & history: O sons of Jacob, His chosen ones
You are God's chosen one among us
Psalms & wisdom: O sons of Jacob, His chosen ones
that I may see the prosperity of Your chosen ones
The Prophets: My elect will possess My mountains
You will leave behind your name as a curse for My chosen ones
My chosen ones will fully enjoy the work of their hands
Gospels & Acts: for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short
to deceive even the elect, if that were possible
they will gather His elect from the four winds
for the sake of the elect, whom He has chosen
to deceive even the elect, if that were possible
to gather His elect from the four winds
His elect who cry out to Him day and night
The letters: Who will bring any charge against God's elect?
What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did
as the elect of God, holy and beloved
I endure all things for the sake of the elect
To the elect who are exiles of the Dispersion
To the chosen lady and her children

rows.alike: "His chosen ones" (1 Chronicles 16:13, Psalm 105:6), "My elect" and "My chosen ones" (Isaiah 65), "the elect" and "His elect" (the Gospels), "God's elect" (Romans 8:33, Titus 1:1).
rows.different: Chronicles and the Psalm set the words beside "O sons of Jacob", and Isaiah 65:9 beside "descendants from Jacob, and heirs from Judah"; in Matthew and Mark the days are cut short "for the sake of the elect", and Luke 18:7 has "His elect who cry out to Him day and night". Romans 11:7 has "What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did"; Colossians 3:12 addresses its readers "as the elect of God" and 1 Peter 1:1 "To the elect who are exiles".

rows.title: Called and chosen

The Prophets: called you from its farthest corners
I have chosen and not rejected you
Gospels & Acts: For many are called, but few are chosen
The letters: consider the time of your calling
But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise
Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light
strive to make your calling and election sure
Revelation: He will be accompanied by His called and chosen and faithful ones

rows.alike: Being called and being chosen stand together: "many are called, but few are chosen", "His called and chosen and faithful ones", "your calling and election", and in Isaiah 41:9 "called you" with "I have chosen".
rows.different: Isaiah 41:9 has a "you" who is told "You are My servant"; Matthew 22:14 has "many are called, but few are chosen"; Revelation 17:14 has "His called and chosen and faithful ones" with the Lamb. 2 Peter 1:10 tells its readers to "make your calling and election sure", and 1 Corinthians 1 says "God chose the foolish things of the world".

rows.title: Those who call on the name of the LORD

The Law & history: At that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD
There he built an altar to the LORD, and he called on the name of the LORD
there Abram called on the name of the LORD
there he called upon the name of the LORD, the Eternal God
So Isaac built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD
I will call on the name of the LORD
call on the name of the LORD his God
called on the name of Baal from morning until noon
You must not call on the names of their gods
I will call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised; so shall I be saved from my enemies
Psalms & wisdom: the kingdoms that refuse to call on Your name
we will call on Your name
Samuel was among those who called on His name
Then I called on the name of the LORD
I will lift the cup of salvation and call on the name of the LORD
call on the name of the LORD
they refuse to call upon the LORD
I will call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised; so shall I be saved from my enemies
The Prophets: No one calls on Your name
the families that do not call on Your name
I called on Your name, O LORD, out of the depths of the Pit
everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved
that all may call upon the name of the LORD and serve Him shoulder to shoulder
They will call on My name, and I will answer them
Gospels & Acts: everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved
to arrest all who call on Your name
those who call on this name
The letters: gives richly to all who call on Him
Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved
all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ
Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity
together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart

rows.alike: "everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved" (Joel 2:32), "everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved" (Acts 2:21) and "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved" (Romans 10:13); from Genesis to the Prophets people "call on the name of the LORD"; 2 Samuel 22:4 and Psalm 18:3 have "I will call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised; so shall I be saved from my enemies".
rows.different: In Genesis the calling is at an altar: "he built an altar to the LORD, and he called on the name of the LORD"; Psalm 116 joins it to "the cup of salvation". Psalm 79 and Jeremiah 10 speak of nations "that refuse" or "do not call on Your name", and Psalm 14:4 says of the workers of iniquity "they refuse to call upon the LORD". Acts 9:14 speaks of authority "to arrest all who call on Your name"; 1 Corinthians 1:2 names "our Lord Jesus Christ", and 2 Timothy 2:19 has "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity".

rows.title: Those far off and those near

Psalms & wisdom: better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away
The Prophets: You who are far off, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge My might
Peace, peace to those far and near
all Israel near and far, in all the countries to which You have driven us
He who is far off will die by the plague, he who is near will fall by the sword
and not a God far away?
Gospels & Acts: This promise belongs to you and your children and to all who are far off
The letters: you who once were far away have been brought near through the blood of Christ
He came and preached peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near

rows.alike: "Peace, peace to those far and near" (Isaiah 57:19) and "peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near" (Ephesians 2:17); Isaiah 33:13 calls to "You who are far off" and "you who are near", and Acts 2:39 has "to all who are far off".
rows.different: Isaiah 33:13 calls both to "hear" and "acknowledge My might"; Daniel 9:7 speaks of "all Israel near and far", scattered "in all the countries to which You have driven us", and Ezekiel 6:12 of plague for the one "far off" and sword for the one "near". Acts 2:39 gives "This promise" to "you and your children" and the far off; Ephesians 2:13 says the far "have been brought near through the blood of Christ".

rows.title: The gates of death, of Sheol, of Hades

Psalms & wisdom: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
Lift me up from the gates of death
They loathed all food and drew near to the gates of death
The Prophets: In the prime of my life I must go through the gates of Sheol
Gospels & Acts: the gates of Hades will not prevail against it

rows.alike: "the gates of death" (Job 38:17, Psalms 9:13 and 107:18), "the gates of Sheol" (Isaiah 38:10), "the gates of Hades" (Matthew 16:18).
rows.different: In the Psalms and Isaiah the gates are what one nears or must pass through: "Lift me up from the gates of death", "drew near to the gates of death", "I must go through the gates of Sheol"; Job 38:17 asks "Have the gates of death been revealed to you?" Matthew 16:18 says of "My church" that "the gates of Hades will not prevail against it".

rows.title: Head over all; the head of the body

The Law & history: You are exalted as head over all
will be the head of all who live in Gilead
The letters: made Him head over everything for the church
grow up into Christ Himself, who is the head
the husband is the head of the wife as Christ is the head of the church, His body
He is the head of the body, the church
who is the head over every ruler and authority
the head, from whom the whole body, supported and knit together by its joints and ligaments, grows as God causes it to grow
the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God

rows.alike: "head over all" (1 Chronicles 29:11), "head over everything" (Ephesians 1:22), "the head over every ruler and authority" (Colossians 2:10).
rows.different: 1 Chronicles 29:11 is addressed "O LORD" and set beside "Yours, O LORD, is the kingdom"; the letters say it of Christ and add the body: "He is the head of the body, the church", "the head, from whom the whole body" grows. Ephesians 5:23 sets it beside "the husband is the head of the wife", and 1 Corinthians 11:3 has "the head of Christ is God".

rows.title: That they may be one; one body

The Prophets: I will give them one heart and one way
join them together into one stick, so that they become one in your hand
they will become one in My hand
I will make them one nation in the land
Gospels & Acts: to gather them together into one
so that they may be one as We are one
that all of them may be one
so that they may be one as We are one
that they may be perfectly united
The multitude of believers was one in heart and soul
The letters: each of us has one body with many members
so in Christ we who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another
Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body
although its parts are many, they all form one body
For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body
there are many parts, but one body
Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it
you are all one in Christ Jesus
who has made the two one
to create in Himself one new man out of the two
reconciling both of them to God in one body
There is one body and one Spirit
For we are members of His body
His body, which is the church
you were called as members of one body
you also died to the law through the body of Christ
a participation in the body of Christ

rows.alike: More than one become one: "they become one in your hand" (Ezekiel 37:17), "that all of them may be one" (John 17:21), "we who are many are one body" (Romans 12:5, 1 Corinthians 10:17), "who has made the two one" (Ephesians 2:14).
rows.different: Ezekiel 37 says it of "the stick of Joseph" and "the stick of Judah", that they "will no longer be two nations"; John 17 is a prayer, "that all of them may be one, as You, Father, are in Me"; Acts 4:32 says "one in heart and soul". The letters say "one body" and "the body of Christ"; Galatians 3:28 lists "neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female" and says "you are all one in Christ Jesus", 1 Corinthians 10:17 joins "one body" to "one loaf", and 1 Corinthians 12:13 to "one Spirit".

rows.title: One Father

The Prophets: Do we not all have one Father? Did not one God create us?
Gospels & Acts: you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers
for you have one Father, who is in heaven
The letters: yet for us there is but one God, the Father
one Lord, one faith, one baptism
one God and Father of all

rows.alike: "one Father" (Malachi 2:10, Matthew 23:9), "one God, the Father" (1 Corinthians 8:6), "one God and Father of all" (Ephesians 4:6).
rows.different: Malachi 2:10 draws from it "Why then do we break faith with one another"; Matthew 23 draws "you are all brothers" and "do not call anyone on earth your father". Malachi sets "one Father" beside "one God create us"; 1 Corinthians 8:6 sets "one God, the Father" beside "one Lord, Jesus Christ", and Ephesians 4:5 has "one Lord, one faith, one baptism".

rows.title: The bridegroom and his bride

The Law & history: you are a bridegroom of blood to me
as was customary for the bridegroom
as a bride returning to her husband
Psalms & wisdom: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride
You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride

Like a bridegroom emerging from his chamber
The Prophets: your land will be His bride

the voices of a bride and bridegroom will never call out in you again

rows.alike: A bridegroom is set beside his bride: "as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride" (Isaiah 62:5), "The bride belongs to the bridegroom" (John 3:29), "His bride has made herself ready" (Revelation 19:7).
rows.different: In Isaiah, Jeremiah and Hosea the words are spoken to "you": "so your God will rejoice over you", "your love as a bride, how you followed Me", "I will betroth you to Me forever"; Jeremiah 2:32 adds "Yet My people have forgotten Me". In the Song they are the lover's: "my sister, my bride". In the Gospels "the bridegroom will be taken from them" and "was delayed"; Revelation names "the bride, the wife of the Lamb" and has "The Spirit and the bride say".

rows.title: Your husband is your Maker; Christ and the church

The Prophets: For your husband is your Maker-the LORD of Hosts is His name
like a wife deserted and wounded in spirit

though I was a husband to them

The letters: I promised you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave Himself up for her
to present her to Himself as a glorious church, without stain or wrinkle or any such blemish, but holy and blameless
I am speaking about Christ and the church

rows.alike: Each speaks of a husband: "your husband is your Maker", "I was a husband to them", "I promised you to one husband", "just as Christ loved the church".
rows.different: Isaiah 54:5 names the husband as "the LORD of Hosts"; Jeremiah 3:20 speaks of a woman who may betray her husband, "so you have betrayed Me, O house of Israel"; Ezekiel 16:32 says to an "adulterous wife", "You receive strangers instead of your own husband!"; and in Hosea 2:7 she says "I will return to my first husband". 2 Corinthians 11:2 has "to present you as a pure virgin to Christ", and Ephesians 5:27 "to present her to Himself as a glorious church, without stain or wrinkle"; Ephesians 5 sets "Husbands, love your wives" beside "Christ loved the church" and says "I am speaking about Christ and the church".

rows.title: His flock and its shepherds

Psalms & wisdom: we Your people, the sheep of Your pasture
we are the people of His pasture, the sheep under His care

The Prophets: I will give you shepherds after My own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding
Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of My pasture!

Gospels & Acts: Do not be afraid, little flock

rows.alike: "the sheep of His pasture" (Psalm 100:3) and "the sheep of My pasture" (Jeremiah 23:1, Ezekiel 34:31); those set over the flock are to feed or shepherd it: "Should not the shepherds feed their flock?", "Shepherd My sheep", "Be shepherds of God's flock".
rows.different: In the Psalms the people say it of themselves, "we are His people"; in Jeremiah and Ezekiel God speaks of "My flock" and of shepherds who "destroy and scatter". In John 21 the charge is given to "Simon Peter": "Feed My lambs", "Shepherd My sheep"; Acts 20:28 says "the Holy Spirit has made you overseers", and 1 Peter 5:3 adds "not lording it over those entrusted to you".

rows.title: Seventy elders; elders in each church

The Law & history: Bring Me seventy of the elders of Israel known to you as leaders and officers of the people

rows.different: In Numbers 11:16 the LORD tells Moses "Bring Me seventy of the elders of Israel known to you as leaders and officers of the people"; in Acts 14:23 "Paul and Barnabas appointed elders", "praying and fasting", and Titus 1:5 has "as I directed you". Acts 15 names "the apostles and elders" together; James 5:14 has the sick "call the elders of the church to pray over him"; 1 Peter 5:1 writes "As a fellow elder".

rows.title: Love one another

Gospels & Acts: A new commandment I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you also must love one another.

The letters: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love

rows.alike: "Love one another" (John 13:34, 15:17) and "we should love one another" (1 John 3:11, 3:23); "a new commandment" in John 13:34 and 1 John 2:8.
rows.different: John 13:34 has "A new commandment I give you" and John 15:12 "This is My commandment", both with "as I have loved you"; 1 John 2:7 says "not writing to you a new commandment, but an old one", and 2 John 1:5 "not as a new commandment to you, but one we have had from the beginning". John 13:35 makes it the mark by which "everyone will know that you are My disciples"; 1 John 4:11 grounds it in "if God so loved us", and 1 Thessalonians 4:9 says "taught by God to love one another".

rows.title: Speak truth to one another

The Law & history: You must not lie or deceive one another.
Psalms & wisdom: They lie to one another; they speak with flattering lips and a double heart.
The Prophets: Speak truth to one another, render true and sound judgments in your gates

rows.alike: Bread is taken, a blessing spoken or thanks given, and the bread broken: "took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it" (Matthew 26:26, Mark 14:22, Luke 24:30), "took the bread, gave thanks and broke it" (Luke 22:19), "took bread and gave thanks" (Acts 27:35), "when He had given thanks, He broke it" (1 Corinthians 11:24); "the breaking of the bread" stands in Luke 24:35 and "the breaking of bread" in Acts 2:42.
rows.different: In the feedings it is "the loaves" that are broken and given "to the people"; in Matthew 26, Mark 14, Luke 22 and 1 Corinthians 11 the words go on "this is My body" or "This is My body", and Luke and 1 Corinthians add "do this in remembrance of Me".
